detailedExplanation: During exercise, muscle cells contract more frequently and need more energy. Respiration rate therefore increases. The body responds by increasing heart rate, breathing rate and breathing depth, bringing more oxygen and glucose to muscles and removing carbon dioxide faster.

If oxygen delivery is insufficient, some anaerobic respiration occurs and lactic acid accumulates. After exercise, additional oxygen is needed to deal with the lactic acid and restore normal conditions. Lactic acid is transported in the blood to the liver where it can be converted back into glucose.
